curated.background:
Source. MathOverflow question 476077, asked by Nathaniel Johnston on 30 July 2024: https://mathoverflow.net/questions/476077/bounding-elementary-symmetric-polynomials-away-from-zero

Known partial results. In the post the poser states that the conjecture holds when all entries of $x$ are nonnegative, hence when $m = n$; that the case $k = 1$ is trivial; and that the bound is attained at the vector with $m-1$ entries equal to $1/(m-1)$ and all other entries equal to $0$. The question has no answer. Its comments discuss the inequalities of Newton and Maclaurin without reaching a proof.

A web search on 2026-11-11 found no paper stating or resolving this inequality.

lean_target.correspondence: x is a real vector indexed by Fin n. e_k(x) is Multiset.esymm k of the multiset of its entries: the sum, over all k-element sub-multisets, of the product of their entries. The hypotheses are 2 ≤ m ≤ n, every entry at most 1/(m-1), e_1(x) = 1, and e_k(x) ≥ 0 for 1 ≤ k ≤ m. The conclusion is e_k(x) ≥ C(m-1, k) / (m-1)^k for every k with 1 ≤ k < m.
lean_target.text:
import Mathlib

def wishpool_target_prop : Prop :=
  ∀ (m n : ℕ) (x : Fin n → ℝ), 2 ≤ m → m ≤ n →
    (∀ j, x j ≤ 1 / ((m : ℝ) - 1)) →
    (Finset.univ.val.map x).esymm 1 = 1 →
    (∀ k, 1 ≤ k → k ≤ m → 0 ≤ (Finset.univ.val.map x).esymm k) →
    ∀ k, 1 ≤ k → k < m →
      ((m - 1).choose k : ℝ) / ((m : ℝ) - 1) ^ k ≤ (Finset.univ.val.map x).esymm k

curated.name: Johnston's conjectured lower bound for elementary symmetric polynomials of real vectors (MathOverflow 476077)

curated.statement:
Let $2 \le m \le n$ be integers and let $x = (x_1, \dots, x_n)$ be a real vector whose entries may be negative. Write $e_k(x)$ for the $k$-th elementary symmetric polynomial of $x$. Assume that

$$\max_j x_j \le \frac{1}{m-1}, \qquad e_1(x) = 1, \qquad e_k(x) \ge 0 \ \text{ for } 1 \le k \le m.$$

Conjecture. Then

$$e_k(x) \ge \binom{m-1}{k} \frac{1}{(m-1)^k} \qquad \text{for all } 1 \le k < m.$$
